segments.name: Consumer
segments.job: Give me a correct answer on health, money or law, and say when you are unsure.

segments.name: Developer
segments.job: Finish the task inside the scope I set, and prove it with a real test run.

segments.name: Enterprise
segments.job: Show which AI uses pay back, without our data leaving our control.

use: Treat any answer you will repeat to a client as unchecked until two key claims match a quoted sentence on the page.
Use deep research mode for multi-part questions, and ask for the plan first.
End with: list the searches you ran, the pages you opened, and anything that failed.
Paste or upload the source yourself when it matters, especially paywalled pages and PDFs.
Never give a browsing agent your email, payments or private files.
build: Measure a baseline on your own questions first. Agree a ceiling on what each run may cost.
Ship the failure ledger and zero-source rule next. Continue only if silent failures fall.
Run domain allow and block lists on every answer. Add read-before-cite and a citation checker to anything forwarded.
Show source labels beside every check mark. A quote from a planted page still passes the check.
If the agent can act, read pages in a separate model with no tools. Read-only research can use filters.
consumer: Check any health, money or legal answer with a qualified person before acting.
Ask for the best case against your view. Agreement is not evidence.
Keep company and private data out of personal AI accounts.
Note your plan's limits and model, and check them again after each update.
Restate key facts and rules at the start of long chats.
developer: Give agents the least access they need, with no production access or saved passwords.
Require an approval step before any delete or deploy.
Accept "tests pass" only with a test log the tool captured.
Pin model versions and rerun your own tests before any upgrade.
Treat repos, plug-ins and tool settings as untrusted, and patch agent tools quickly.
enterprise: Who: the CIO. First step: give staff one approved AI tool, with controls that stop company data leaving.
Who: the finance lead. First step: for each AI project, compare what it saves with what it costs. Agree the rule for stopping it before it starts.
Who: the security lead. First step: list every AI tool that can act on its own. Make sure every action is recorded and it can be switched off. Test the switch.
Who: the procurement lead. First step: add notice periods to AI contracts for when a vendor retires the AI version you use, and for changes to usage limits.
Who: the HR lead, with team managers. First step: work out how many people are needed to check AI work, and shape roles around that volume.
Who: the head of each team that sends AI work outside the company. First step: name one person who checks every figure, quote and source before it is sent.
